analysis.title: From panic to the next squeeze? NVDA nosedives, shorts surge, India impresses
key_insights: NVDA fell nearly 40% from its early October ATH at today's lows, approaching the Liberation Day drawdown (which exceeded 40% but unfolded more slowly). It traded nearly 30% below its 200-day MA, matching the Liberation Day undershoot.

Goldman's Jim Schneider compares Nvidia to Apple during Steve Jobs' 2011 departure. Apple's forward P/E compressed from 17x to 12x and bottomed near 9x in 2013 before recovering. Schneider expects a similar period of multiple uncertainty for Nvidia but sees attractive risk/reward given Goldman's forecast of roughly 80% EPS growth.
Before the latest selloff, NVDA had fallen to its cheapest valuation versus the S&P 500 in almost 25 years.
Nvidia's share of Chinese data-center AI accelerator shipments fell to 34% in H1 2026, with Huawei at 28%. TS Lombard argues US export restrictions are accelerating China's domestic AI ecosystem.

JPM says QQQ short interest is at its highest since 2023 and Nasdaq futures positioning has been heavily reduced. Hedge funds entered the November selloff already having cut significant exposure, which leaves potential incremental demand if the market stabilizes. Some of the QQQ short interest may be hedges against existing longs.

JPM estimates the momentum long/short factor is down about 40% from its peak, the largest unwind since the post-GFC recovery. October's 11% decline in the long momentum-versus-market portfolio was roughly a six-sigma event. Short-term crowding measures are near historical extremes.

JPM argues hedge funds have largely finished de-risking. Continued retail support could stabilize AI stocks through November and let hedge funds rebuild positions from late November onward, adding a second wave of demand.

TS Lombard says foreign investors put about $6.5B into Indian equities in November so far, after heavy selling through most of 2026. India is the best-performing emerging market this month and the Nifty is back to its pre-war February levels.

The Market Ear took profit on its bullish India view from October. The Nifty rallied sharply off range lows into extremely overbought territory, though it has not reached the top of the range. It sees the risk/reward as changed.

Gold volatility is rising as prices fall, the reverse of its usual pattern. Investors are paying up for downside protection and The Market Ear calls the move a disorderly selloff, not an orderly correction.
DXY broke out to its highest since April 2025. The 200-day MA is sloping higher and RSI is well below overbought. The Market Ear sees little resistance until the major trendline around 105.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Schneider sees attractive risk/reward at current levels on roughly 80% forecast EPS growth, despite expected multiple uncertainty like Apple in 2011.

earnings_insights: Goldman forecasts roughly 80% EPS growth for Nvidia (basis not specified in the note).

trade_ideas.rationale: The Nifty rallied aggressively off range lows into extremely overbought territory, so risk/reward has changed.

trade_ideas.description: Long dollar (DXY) on the breakout to the highest since April 2025
trade_ideas.rationale: Momentum is strong, the 200-day MA is sloping higher, RSI is below overbought, and there is little resistance until the trendline around 105.

risk_factors: Further momentum unwind and AI stock selling if retail support fades.
Nvidia multiple compression while leadership and business momentum are unclear.
Loss of China data-center share to Huawei and other domestic suppliers.
Disorderly gold selloff with rising downside-protection demand.
Part of the elevated QQQ short interest may be hedges, which would overstate bearish positioning.
vol_and_positioning: QQQ short interest is at its highest since 2023 (JPM), though part may be hedges against existing longs.
Nasdaq futures positioning has been heavily reduced and hedge fund exposure is well below earlier levels (JPM).
The momentum long/short factor is down about 40% from its peak, with short-term crowding measures near historical extremes (JPM).
Gold implied vol is rising as prices fall, with investors paying up for downside protection.
DXY RSI is well below overbought despite the breakout.
geopolitical: US export restrictions on chips to China are accelerating China's domestic AI chip ecosystem, with Huawei at 28% of Chinese data-center AI accelerator shipments versus Nvidia's 34% in H1 2026 (TS Lombard).
India's equity recovery to pre-war February levels is cited, and the note refers to a prior war.

tension_points.theme: AI stock rebound versus further unwind
tension_points.bull_case: JPM says hedge funds have already de-risked, QQQ shorts are at the highest since 2023, and retail support could stabilize AI stocks through November. Hedge funds could rebuild from late November, adding a second wave of demand. Goldman sees attractive risk/reward on roughly 80% EPS growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Nvidia's multiple may keep compressing as in Apple 2011 (17x to 9x), Nvidia is losing China share to Huawei, and part of the QQQ short interest may be hedges rather than outright bearish bets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail support fading before hedge funds rebuild positions in late November.
